actions.justification: Patient presents with 'cold-wet' ADHF profile: confusion, cold extremities, low BP (85/55), and SpO2 88%. Assessing perfusion status is the critical first step to confirm cardiogenic/low-output state and guide inotrope vs. vasopressor decision.
Concurrent volume status assessment is essential in cold-wet ADHF to quantify congestion severity and guide whether diuresis is safe given the low MAP and potential cardiogenic shock.
BMP is urgently needed to evaluate renal function, electrolytes, and lactate-surrogate markers before initiating inotropes or diuretics in this hypotensive, low-perfusion state.

Patient is 'cold and wet' with MAP 65, BP 85/55, HR 110, SpO2 88%, and signs of poor perfusion (confusion, cold extremities). This is consistent with cardiogenic shock. AHA guidelines recommend considering inotropes within 60 minutes for ADHF cold-wet. Vasodilators and high-dose diuretics are relatively contraindicated given hypotension; inotropic support is the priority.
BNP should be ordered within 60 minutes per AHA guideline time-critical actions to confirm heart failure diagnosis and assess severity. Not yet completed.

This patient has cardiogenic shock (cold-wet ADHF, BP 85/55, MAP 65, SpO2 88%) and requires urgent cardiology input for advanced management decisions including potential ICU admission and vasopressor/mechanical support considerations.
Troponin is essential to rule out acute myocardial infarction as a precipitant of this decompensated heart failure with cardiogenic shock presentation. ACS is a common trigger for cold-wet ADHF.
Chest X-ray will assess degree of pulmonary congestion and edema in this cold-wet ADHF patient with SpO2 88% and severe dyspnea, guiding diuretic therapy decisions.

Echocardiogram is indicated per AHA guidelines (within 1440 min) to assess cardiac function, ejection fraction, wall motion abnormalities, and guide management in this patient with HFrEF in decompensated state with cardiogenic shock features.

Patient presents with ADHF cold-wet phenotype with severe dyspnea, hypoxia (SpO2 88%), and signs of volume overload. IV diuretics are indicated to reduce preload and relieve pulmonary congestion. Although systolic BP is low (85 mmHg), diuresis addresses the 'wet' component of the cold-wet profile. Monitor closely given low BP.

Vasodilators can reduce afterload and improve forward flow in ADHF cold-wet when used cautiously. However, given the BP of 85/55 mmHg (MAP 65), this must be used with extreme caution and only if perfusion improves with inotropic support already initiated. Guideline contraindicates vasodilators when SBP <90 mmHg per nitroglycerin contraindication table — reconsider if BP does not respond.
Mandatory action not yet completed - obtain targeted history of HF exacerbation triggers, medication compliance, fluid intake, and symptom timeline in this cold/wet ADHF patient.
Mandatory action not yet completed - systematic physical exam to assess JVP, S3 gallop, peripheral edema, lung crackles, and perfusion status in this hemodynamically compromised patient.
Mandatory action with 60-minute deadline - ECG required to identify arrhythmias (HR 110), ischemia, or conduction abnormalities contributing to decompensated HFrEF.
Mandatory action: BMP needed to assess electrolytes, renal function, and glucose in this diabetic patient with cardiogenic shock presentation.
Mandatory action: BNP/NT-proBNP needed to quantify degree of heart failure and guide management, per AHA guidelines with 60-min deadline.

Patient has cardiogenic shock features (BP 85/55, confusion, cold extremities, SpO2 88%). AHA guidelines mandate ICU admission within 30 min for cardiogenic shock management. This is critically needed.
